plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Southern Hemisphere cities turn misty violet when this tree flowers. Clusters of trumpet-shaped blooms open on feathery, fern-like foliage. They carpet pavements in purple as they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (October to December) in the Southern Hemisphere, with a peak in November
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and eastern Australia, including Sydney and Brisbane
plants.funFact: Native to South America, jacaranda has become a signature tree of Pretoria, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. Its seed pods are flat and woody, and they rattle in the wind.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub brings color to the cool, quiet days of late autumn. Its delicate, lightly scented flowers open wide to show golden stamens. Bees visit them on mild days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Southern Japan, and gardens in the southeastern United States and Mediterranean-climate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Oil pressed from its seeds has long been used in Japan for cooking and for hair care.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is South Africa's national flower. It has a dramatic bowl-shaped head, up to 30 cm across, ringed with silky pink bracts around a crown of fuzzy centers. It grows on rocky fynbos slopes and is tough and long-lasting.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer, with peak flowering from about November to January
plants.location: Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa (fynbos region)
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient plant family that dates back to the time of Gondwana. The genus is named for the Greek sea god Proteus, who could change shape, because the plants vary so much in form.
